transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you for seeing me. I, um... I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time. I guess what finally pushed me to come in is just... well, my eating has been a little all over the place lately. I mean, it's probably nothing major, just normal stress, right? But some weeks I barely touch dinner at all. And then other nights, I find myself standing in the kitchen eating crackers and sweets after everyone else has gone to bed. It's a little embarrassing to admit, honestly. Is that... is that something that makes sense to bring up?
When you eat those crackers and sweets at night, do you feel like you lose control over how much you’re eating?

Oh, no, no... I wouldn't say I lose control. I mean, it's really just a handful of crackers here and there. I can stop whenever I want to, I promise. It's just... I guess I just get a little peckish when the house is quiet? 

I'm definitely not, like, gorging myself or doing anything extreme. I hope I didn't make it sound worse than it actually is... I just wanted to be thorough for you. I'm just having a normal snack, really. Does that make sense?
Do you ever try to avoid eating or eat much less because of your weight or how your body looks?

Oh, no... no, definitely not. I mean, I'm not really focused on my weight or anything like that. I'm pretty comfortable with how I look, honestly. I definitely don't try to, um, avoid eating just to be thin or anything. 

I hope I didn't give you the impression that I'm obsessed with my body or doing anything unhealthy on purpose... it's really just that my appetite gets a little unpredictable sometimes. That's a pretty normal thing, right? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
When you have those nighttime eating episodes, do you feel a sense of loss of control over what or how much you’re eating?

Um, I think... I think maybe you asked me that a minute ago? But, um, no, I definitely don't lose control. I'm really sorry if I'm repeating myself or if I didn't explain it well the first time! I just want to make sure I'm answering exactly what you need. 

But yes, it's just a small snack, really. I can always stop when I want to. I'm not doing anything, you know, out of hand. I hope that's the right answer? I just don't want you to worry that I'm doing something unhealthy.
Do these nighttime eating episodes happen at least once a week?

Um, well... I guess they do happen maybe once a week, or, you know, sometimes a little more. But it's really not every single night! I just... I think what really pushed me to finally make this appointment and come in is just that my eating has been a little... all over the place lately. 

Like, some weeks I'll barely even touch my dinner, and then other nights I'll just find myself standing in the kitchen having those crackers and sweets after everyone else is asleep. I know that probably sounds a little silly, right? I just wanted to be completely honest with you about it. I hope it doesn't make me sound too chaotic... I'm really trying to keep a good routine. Is that the kind of thing you were looking for?
After those nighttime eating episodes, do you ever do anything to try to make up for it, like vomiting, using laxatives, or exercising extra?

Oh, no, definitely not! I would never do anything like that. I mean, I know some people struggle with those kinds of things, but I promise I don't do any of that. No vomiting or laxatives or anything extreme. 

I just... I just go back to bed, really. I don't want you to think I'm doing anything dangerous or, um, hurting myself to make up for a little snack. It's really just a few crackers, so there's no need to do anything drastic, you know? I hope that reassures you... I'm really trying to take good care of myself.
Have these eating changes been causing you significant distress?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say distress. Not at all. I mean... I feel a little silly even bringing it up, honestly. It's really just a minor thing. I don't want you to think I'm, you know, falling apart over a few crackers or anything! 

It's completely manageable. I just thought I should mention it so you have all the right information... I hope that makes sense? I really try not to make a fuss over the little things, so it's definitely not causing me any real trouble. I hope I didn't make it sound worse than it actually is!
Have you lost or gained a significant amount of weight because of these eating changes?

Um, well, no, not really. I haven't noticed any big changes on the scale or anything. Like I mentioned earlier, the whole reason I brought it up is just that my eating is a bit... all over the place. You know, barely touching dinner some weeks, and then doing the whole crackers and sweets thing in the kitchen late at night. 

But it really hasn't affected my weight much at all! I think it all just balances out in the end. I hope that's okay? I really don't want you to worry that my health is suffering or anything. I'm doing my best to keep everything stable.
During those nighttime episodes, do you ever eat an unusually large amount of food in a short period of time?

Oh, goodness, no. Definitely not a large amount. Um... it's really just, like I said, a few crackers or maybe a little piece of something sweet. I'm just grabbing a tiny snack, not... not emptying the pantry or anything like that. 

I know eating late isn't the best habit, but I always make sure to keep it under control. I really try to be good about that. I hope that's okay? I promise I'm not overdoing it or losing control. I just want to make sure I'm doing the right thing, you know?
When this happens at night, do you eat what most people would consider a large amount of food in a short period of time?

Oh, no, definitely not. I mean, I think you actually just asked me that, didn't you? I'm sorry if I wasn't clear before! But no, it's really just a tiny bit. Like, literally just a couple of crackers to settle my stomach, or a small bite of chocolate. 

I would never eat a huge amount like that. I know that wouldn't be healthy, and I really try to take good care of myself. I hope I'm explaining it right? I just want to make sure you know I'm not doing anything extreme or out of control. It's just a little nibble, I promise.
When you wake up and find yourself eating at night, are you fully awake and aware of it?

Oh, yes, I'm completely awake. It's not like sleepwalking or anything scary like that. I just wake up, realize I'm a little hungry, and go to the kitchen. I'm totally aware of what I'm doing the whole time. 

I know some people do things in their sleep, but I promise I'm fully conscious and just getting a tiny snack. I hope that makes sense? I wouldn't want you to think I was doing things without realizing it. I'm always very careful.
During the day, do you often skip meals or intentionally eat much less than you think you should?

Well, um... I wouldn't say I intentionally starve myself or anything bad like that. I really do try to eat normally. But... I guess, honestly, that's kind of what finally pushed me to come in to see you. My eating has just been a little... all over the place lately. 

Like, some weeks I just don't have much of an appetite, and I might barely touch my dinner. I don't mean to, I just don't feel hungry. But then, like I was saying before, other nights I'll find myself standing in the kitchen having those crackers and sweets after everyone else has gone to bed. 

It's a little embarrassing to admit that it fluctuates so much. I know I should be more consistent, and I really want to be. I hope you don't think I'm being careless with my health? I'm really trying to figure out why it's been so uneven lately. Does that sound like something we can work on?
Do you usually eat most of your food after dinner or at night?

Oh, no, no, definitely not. I mean, even when my appetite is a bit... unpredictable, I still make sure to have my actual meals during the day. Like a normal person, you know? I'll have breakfast, or at least a proper lunch. 

The night time is really just... just those little nibbles I mentioned before. I really try hard to keep a regular schedule so I'm not eating everything in the dark. I wouldn't want you to think my whole routine is completely upside down or that I'm completely nocturnal! I'm doing my best to stay on a normal daytime schedule with my meals... I hope that's what I'm supposed to be doing?
Do you wake up from sleep specifically to eat at night?

Oh, no, it's not like that. I don't go to sleep and then... suddenly wake up just because I need to eat. That sounds a little out of control, doesn't it? 

It's more like... if I happen to wake up to use the restroom, or if I just can't sleep and I'm tossing and turning, then I might realize I'm a tiny bit hungry. But the sleep interrupting comes first, not the food. I promise I'm not setting an alarm to go eat or anything strange like that. I hope that makes it sound a little better? I just don't want you to think I have some kind of terrible eating problem on top of everything else.
Do you ever feel that your self-worth is strongly tied to your weight or body shape?

Oh, um... no, I wouldn't say that. I mean, of course, I think everyone wants to look nice and feel good in their clothes, right? But I don't think my whole worth as a person is tied to the scale or anything like that. 

I really try to focus on just being a good person and, you know, being kind. I know it's not healthy to obsess over weight, so I do my best to keep a balanced perspective. I hope that's the right way to look at it? I definitely don't want to seem superficial or like I'm overly focused on my appearance.
When you wake up at night, do you feel like you need to eat in order to fall back asleep?

Um... well, I wouldn't say I absolutely *have* to eat just to fall back asleep. I really try not to make it a habit. But... I guess I should just be honest with you, since it's actually what finally pushed me to come in and get some help. 

My eating has just been kind of... all over the place lately. I'm a little embarrassed to admit it, but some weeks I barely touch my dinner at all. And then... well, other nights, I'll find myself just standing in the kitchen, eating crackers and sweets after everyone else has gone to bed. I know it's not a good thing to do, and I'm really trying to be better about it. I just want to get back on a normal track... I hope you don't think too badly of me for that?
When you eat these crackers and sweets at night, do you ever feel like you can’t stop once you start?

Oh, goodness, no. I mean... I definitely don't lose control or anything like that. It's really just a few crackers or a small piece of something sweet, and then I make sure to put the box right back in the pantry. I definitely know when to stop. 

I really try to be mindful of it, even when I'm up late and feeling a little out of sorts. I wouldn't just keep eating and eating... that would be terrible, wouldn't it? I just have a little bite and then I go wash my hands and head right back to bed. I promise I'm not overdoing it. I hope you believe me? I really am trying to keep things as normal and healthy as I can.
When you wake up at night and go to the kitchen, do you feel fully awake the whole time?

Oh, yes, definitely. I'm completely awake. I mean, I know what I'm doing when I get up. It's not like I'm sleepwalking or in some kind of daze or anything strange like that. 

I just... I wake up, and I know I'm awake, and I just go get a little snack and then go right back. I'm very aware of everything. I wouldn't want you to think I'm doing things without realizing it, you know? That sounds so scary. I'm fully conscious and in control... that's a good thing, right?
When you eat at night, is it because you feel a strong urge or compulsion to eat, even if you didn’t plan to?

No, no, it's not a compulsion or anything intense like that. I don't want you to think I'm just... acting on these wild urges. It's really just that I happen to be awake, and I think, "Oh, maybe a little cracker would be nice." 

It's very casual, really. I'm not driven to do it against my will or anything. I just... I decide to have a tiny bite, and that's it. It's perfectly normal to have a small snack if you're up, isn't it? I just want to make sure I'm doing things the right way... I'm not doing anything too concerning, am I?
On most days, do you eat a large portion of your calories after the evening meal or at night?

Oh, no, definitely not. I mean... I still eat my regular meals during the day, just like I'm supposed to. Breakfast, lunch, and a sensible dinner. 

Those little snacks at night, they're just... they're really just a tiny sliver of what I eat all day. Just a cracker or two, like I said. I wouldn't want to ruin my diet or do anything unhealthy by eating too much right before bed. That's really bad for your digestion, isn't it? I try very hard to eat most of my food during the day, when I'm active. I think I'm doing pretty well with that, don't you think?

patient.answer:
Oh, yes, definitely. I'm completely awake. I mean, I know what I'm doing when I get up. It's not like I'm sleepwalking or in some kind of daze or anything strange like that. 

I just... I wake up, and I know I'm awake, and I just go get a little snack and then go right back. I'm very aware of everything. I wouldn't want you to think I'm doing things without realizing it, you know? That sounds so scary. I'm fully conscious and in control... that's a good thing, right?

doctor.intent: Clarify whether the nighttime eating is driven by a true drive to eat large amounts with loss of control, which would support a binge-type disorder rather than a nonspecific eating disturbance
doctor.question: When you eat at night, is it because you feel a strong urge or compulsion to eat, even if you didn’t plan to?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about compulsive eating or binge eating urges, which is not covered by any specific symptom in my profile beyond the general appetite changes already discussed.

patient.answer:
No, no, it's not a compulsion or anything intense like that. I don't want you to think I'm just... acting on these wild urges. It's really just that I happen to be awake, and I think, "Oh, maybe a little cracker would be nice." 

It's very casual, really. I'm not driven to do it against my will or anything. I just... I decide to have a tiny bite, and that's it. It's perfectly normal to have a small snack if you're up, isn't it? I just want to make sure I'm doing things the right way... I'm not doing anything too concerning, am I?

doctor.intent: Clarify whether the eating episodes occur in the context of a regular daytime pattern versus a markedly delayed sleep/eating schedule, which would help distinguish night eating syndrome from other specified feeding/eating disorder or nonspecific eating disturbance.
doctor.question: On most days, do you eat a large portion of your calories after the evening meal or at night?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the proportion of daily calories consumed at night to evaluate for Night Eating Syndrome, which is not specifically covered by my symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Oh, no, definitely not. I mean... I still eat my regular meals during the day, just like I'm supposed to. Breakfast, lunch, and a sensible dinner. 

Those little snacks at night, they're just... they're really just a tiny sliver of what I eat all day. Just a cracker or two, like I said. I wouldn't want to ruin my diet or do anything unhealthy by eating too much right before bed. That's really bad for your digestion, isn't it? I try very hard to eat most of my food during the day, when I'm active. I think I'm doing pretty well with that, don't you think?

opening_question.intent: To learn the patient’s main reason for seeking care and open the diagnostic interview.
opening_question.question: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports intermittent nighttime snacking and variable appetite, but repeatedly denies binge-sized amounts, loss of control, compensatory behaviors, weight/shape overvaluation, significant distress, or clear nocturnal eating syndrome pattern. The presentation does not meet specific criteria for a defined eating disorder, so the most appropriate code is unspecified eating disorder.
